review_candidates.title: Assistant, Finance & Administration (Beni/Butembo )
review_candidates.company: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies - IFRC
review_candidates.location: Butembo, North Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo
review_candidates.description: Organizational Context The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) is the world’s largest humanitarian network, with 191 National Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies as members. The IFRC draws on the “three Rs” — response, resilience and respect — to implement its Strategy 2030. The IFRC responds to disasters and crises, ensuring rapid, coordinated and locally led humanitarian action. It helps its members strengthen community resilience in climate and environment, health and wellbeing, and migration and displacement. The IFRC promotes respect for its Fundamental Principles of humanity, impartiality, neutrality, independence, voluntary service, unity and universality, including through its work on values, power and inclusion. The IFRC remains focused on its core mandate — its purpose — of strategic and operational coordination, humanitarian diplomacy, National Society development and accountability. The IFRC is led by its Secretary General and has its headquarters in Geneva, as well as five regional offices in Africa (Nairobi), the Americas (Panama), Asia Pacific (Kuala Lumpur), Europe (Budapest) and the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region (Beirut), together with representation offices, service centres and delegations around the world. The IFRC has a zero-tolerance policy towards conduct incompatible with the aims and objectives of the Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment and other forms of harassment, abuse of power, discrimination and lack of integrity (including, but not limited to, financial misconduct). The IFRC also adheres to strict child safeguarding principles. The position will be based in Bunia, Democratic Republic of the Congo, supporting the Ebola response through the field office covering Ituri and neighbouring areas affected by the outbreak. Job Purpose Under the supervision of the Finance and Administration Officer based in Beni/Butembo , the Finance and Administration Assistant provides financial and administrative support to the IFRC in an organised and timely manner. Job Duties And Responsibilities Administration: Work closely with the Finance and Administration Officer to ensure that efficient, high-quality administrative services are provided to cluster users and stakeholders. Contribute to the development and updating of clear and effective administrative procedures for the Office. Ensure that all requested administrative services are provided to users and stakeholders in accordance with established administrative procedures. Ensure the timely delivery of administrative services to Partner National Societies (PNS) at the required quality standards, in accordance with integration or service agreements, and propose appropriate solutions to any challenges encountered. Ensure effective management of information management systems, including electronic and physical filing, reference materials, guidelines and policies, databases and correspondence. Ensure proper management of all contracts, agreements, memoranda of understanding (MoUs) and other legal documents, while maintaining a high level of confidentiality regarding their contents. Manage, maintain and ensure the cleanliness of IFRC premises in accordance with BCP office-cleaning protocols, while ensuring implementation of an environmentally friendly and sustainable strategy. Support local procurement of office supplies, furniture and consumables, promoting the responsible use of resources to reduce waste. Monitor outsourced services provided by suppliers or external agencies and immediately report any deviations from agreed terms of reference to the line manager. Lead local procurement and maintain an up-to-date office-supplies inventory, ensuring adequate stock levels for business continuity. Support the management and administration of contracts and agreements (e.g. annual maintenance contracts (AMCs) for office equipment), in accordance with IFRC procedures, including the electronic contracting process (e-contracting). Maintain a rigorous filing system for all administrative documents to ensure quick and easy access to information. Travel and accommodation arrangements Book short-term accommodation for staff and visitors in hotels and servic Welcoming New Staff/visitors Provide welcome packs to new staff and visitors before their departure. Issue visitor badges to visiting staff and other external guests coming to the office. Invoice Processing Process utility bills for the office and delegates in a timely manner. Process travel agency invoices (air tickets) in a timely manner. Process telecommunications invoices in a timely manner. Process courier service invoices in a timely manner Workshops, Meetings And Conferences Support programmes by coordinating workshops, meetings and conferences. Assist with booking workshop venues with support from the logistics unit. Arrange refreshments and tea breaks for workshops and internal meetings. Assist with setting up meeting rooms. Supervision Monitor outsourced service providers (catering and cleaning companies) daily to ensure high-quality services. Monitor drinking-water supplies and request replenishment from the supplier. Reception Management Provide customer service and respond to all enquiries at reception. Ensure the reception area is clean and tidy. Welcome visitors and direct them to the appropriate offices and staff members. In collaboration with HR, update and circulate the staff contact list every month. Coordinate with relevant departments and staff for receiving and dispatching mail and parcels. Office supplies Filing Job Duties and Responsibilities (continued) Maintain up-to-date administrative files relating to the administrative assistant’s duties and responsibilities. Ensure all important administrative documents and correspondence are filed and stored in a shared location Finance Financial planning and management: Provide support in financial planning, management and resource monitoring to ensure effective and efficient service delivery for the delegation. Financial management Maintain IFRC internal controls and ensure that all transactions are valid and comply with Federation financial procedures. Ensure accounting operations are properly carried out, with financial transactions recorded in the appropriate journals and posted weekly to the ERP financial system to enable timely monthly account closure. Receive supplier invoices, verify supporting documentation and the accuracy of accounting and budget coding, obtain approval from the relevant budget holders and make payments within the required timeframes. Oversee the tracking of rechargeable costs, analyse trends and provide appropriate advice and support. Ensure an effective filing system is established and maintained, guaranteeing a high level of confidentiality for financial documents. Ensure monthly submission of financial statements, perform the necessary reconciliations and provide explanations for the various balance-sheet items. Produce monthly exception reports to support accounting close processes. Coordinate and collaborate with National Societies to obtain their financial reports in accordance with IFRC standards and requirements. Treasury Ensure effective management of funds available for programmes and operations in accordance with organisational policies, and help monitor field bank-account balances to minimise the risk of financial loss. Manage cash and bank payments, ensuring they comply with IFRC procedures and that bank reconciliations are completed and updated monthly. Follow up on the timely submission of cash forecasts (cash requests) by project managers and prepare accurate and timely funding requests. Ensure timely submission of financial reports and draft invoices, including the preparation of integration agreements duly signed by all relevant parties. Financial Advice And Support Support quarterly budget preparation and review, as well as monitoring Shared Office and Services Costs (SOSC). Closely monitor all financial activities and report any risks or potential adverse impacts on internal controls or financial management performance. Maintain up-to-date knowledge of national government requirements and regulations applicable to financial procedures in the country and ensure their implementation. Provide basic training, technical support and guidance to National Societies, programme teams, partners and budget holders to strengthen their skills in budget preparation and monitoring, financial reporting and internal control. Provide necessary training to finance and support staff of Partner National Societies (PNS) on Federation financial management systems, financial management, risk management and audit matters. Also provide general briefings on IFRC policies and guidelines and staff benefits. Support the implementation of audit recommendations. Report any financial irregularities identified and work with the relevant manager to minimise risks. Report any cases or suspected cases of fraud and corruption in accordance with IFRC reporting mechanisms and procedures. Education Degree in Finance and Administration, Logistics, Business Management or another relevant field. Experience At least 2 years of experience in financial and administrative management within a humanitarian organization. Knowledge of and experience with the Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement (Preferred) Ability to work effectively under pressure and manage multiple priorities in a constantly changing environment. Experience in office financial and administrative management, including filing. Experience in finance, administration and other support functions. Experience using financial and administrative procedures and systems. Knowledge, Skills and Languages Ability to work in a multicultural and cross-functional environment. Ability to meet tight deadlines and handle multiple tasks simultaneously. Computer proficiency is essential. Knowledge of ERP systems would be an asset. Excellent communication and report-writing skills. Good interpersonal skills are essential for this position. Proficiency in French and English. Competencies, Values and Comments Values: Respect for diversity; Integrity; Professionalism; Accountability Core competencies: Communication; Collaboration and teamwork; Judgement and decision-making; National Society and customer relations; Creativity and innovation; Building trust

review_candidates.title: General Manager
review_candidates.description: Job Title: General Manager Company: The African Tulip Hotel Location: Arusha, Tanzania (On-site) Website: theafricantulip.co.tz Compensation: US$ 2,000 – 3,000 per month (Net) + Statutory NSSF (~25–30%) + Expatriate Package   About Us Located in a quiet, tree-lined neighborhood in the heart of Arusha, The African Tulip is an intimate, 29-room boutique hotel serving as the premier gateway to Tanzania’s Northern Safari Circuit (Serengeti, Ngorongoro, Tarangire, and Mt. Kilimanjaro). Featuring 22 Deluxe Rooms, 7 Suites, The Baobab Restaurant, Zanzi"bar" Lounge, and Serengeti Pool Bar, we blend warm Tanzanian hospitality with refined, understated luxury for both safari travelers and corporate guests.   The Opportunity This is a long-term leadership role offering a genuine opportunity to build and grow your career within a thriving, expanding East African hospitality market. We are seeking a dynamic, hands-on General Manager who thrives outside the office. This is strictly an independent boutique hotel role —we are looking for a grounded, adaptable operator, not a corporate manager accustomed to large international hotel chains. Working successfully in Africa requires a relentless hands-on approach, consistent follow-ups, and a structured plan to execute daily tasks rather than relying on big-brand bureaucracy or large corporate support teams.   Our Core Hiring Criteria We evaluate every candidate against three non-negotiable pillars: Integrity: Complete honesty regarding operational data, challenges, and personal accountability. Intelligence: Sharp problem-solving ability, cultural adaptability, and commercial awareness. Drive to Get the Job Done: High energy, ownership, and relentless follow-through until daily tasks and standards are executed properly. Key Responsibilities Daily Execution & Follow-Up: Establish clear daily action plans across all departments, ensuring rigorous follow-ups so standards never slip. Hands-On Operational Command: Provide active, daily leadership across Front Office, Housekeeping, F&B, Sales, Engineering, and Security, maintaining high physical visibility on the floor during peak guest hours. Boutique Agility: Design and implement practical, tailored Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) suited for an agile independent property rather than rigid corporate manuals. Revenue & Market Development: Drive occupancy and F&B revenue by leveraging relationships within the Arusha safari circuit, corporate/NGO sectors, and optimizing Online Travel Agencies (OTAs). Training & Mentorship: Act as the primary trainer and mentor for local staff, bridging gaps in formal hospitality education and building long-term capability. Team Unification: Foster a cohesive "one-team" culture by eliminating departmental silos and resolving interpersonal friction before it impacts the guest experience. Qualifications & Experience Independent Hotel Pedigree: 10+ years in hospitality, including 5+ years as a General Manager strictly within independent, boutique, or owner-operated hotels/lodges . (Candidates whose recent background is exclusively in large corporate hotel chains will not be considered). Multi-Departmental Substance: Verifiable track record of working directly across multiple departments—someone who knows how to fix a problem on the ground, not just delegate it. Technical Proficiency: Working knowledge of Property Management Systems (OPERA, IDS, or similar) and full proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, Outlook). Communication: Fluent in English (knowledge of Swahili is an added advantage). Previous work experience in Africa: This will be an advantage but not a determining criteria. Leadership Traits & Mindset Proactive "Owner-Mindset": Possesses a sharp eye for detail to spot maintenance or service flaws before a guest or owner does. Composure & Creative Problem Solving: Remains calm and methodical during unexpected operational challenges (e.g., equipment issues or power outages) and finds resourceful, practical solutions within local constraints. Cultural Intelligence & Diplomacy: Leads a Tanzanian workforce with empathy, respect, and fairness—firm on international standards without being abrasive. Guest-Facing & Approachable: Outgoing personality; genuinely enjoys engaging with guests in the lobby and restaurant to gather feedback and build rapport. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) Guest Satisfaction: Maintaining a 9.0+ rating across major booking platforms. Revenue Growth: Measurable increases in room occupancy and F&B sales. Cost Control: Managing departmental expenses strictly within approved budgetary targets. Staff Retention & Growth: Documented staff training programs and minimal avoidable turnover. Remuneration & Expatriate Benefits Base Salary: US$ 2,000 – 3,000 per month (Net) , commensurate with demonstrated independent hotel experience, with performance-based upward review upon achieving agreed KPIs.
